body: The spec's central inferential machinery is underdetermined in ways that matter. First, the RSS size — the very baseline that defines every sparsity level as a percentage of it — is literally deferred ("a Representative Stratified Sample (RSS) of [deferred] entries"), which makes FR-005's sparsity levels uninterpretable until that number exists; a 10% subset of an unspecified pool is not a defined experiment. Second, the LMM formula `error ~ sparsity_level + (1|seed)` does not actually model the claimed nested structure: a random intercept on seed alone captures between-seed variability in mean error, not the variability in the learning-curve slope between consecutive sparsity levels that FR-007 and SC-003 hinge on; a random slope `(sparsity_level|seed)` or explicit interval-by-seed structure would be needed for 'slope variance' to be a quantity the model can even estimate. Third, the '< 10%' slope-variance threshold is asserted without justification — 10% of what, measured how (coefficient of variation across seeds? change in slope between adjacent levels?) — and SC-003 conflates statistical significance of pairwise level differences (Tukey contrasts) with the magnitude-based diminishing-returns criterion, which are logically distinct tests. Fourth, the spec never states which model is trained across sparsity levels (the project idea names Gaussian Process Regression for uncertainty calibration, and SC-001 logs 'Calibration Slope' and 'Variance', but FR-004's three matminer descriptors and no model-specification requirement leave the calibration pipeline — and hence half the success criteria — undefined. Finally, the test set's relationship to the RSS is unstated: if nested subsets are drawn from the RSS and the test set is also drawn from it, the interpolation/extrapolation distinction motivating the whole study is unaddressed.
